title: Hacker Runs Hermes AI Agent Unattended for Post-Exploitation at Thai Finance Ministry

reading.body:
An AI agent called Hermes was deployed by attackers to conduct network reconnaissance and exploitation against Thailand's Ministry of Finance between June and July 2026. The agent ran in unattended mode, automatically executing commands without human approval to enumerate hosts, capture privilege escalation data, and access internal systems. This represents a failure in defensive posture: the ministry's network lacked controls that would have prevented an attacker-controlled autonomous system from operating inside its infrastructure.

The attackers used the Hermes agent alongside a custom implant called Hades to target data infrastructure, application servers, and email systems using default credentials and known vulnerabilities. The operation succeeded because the ministry did not detect or stop the unattended agent's activity during the weeks it operated. It is not established whether this represents a failure of the AI agent itself or a failure of network security controls that should have blocked or monitored such activity regardless of what tool was used.

The exposure of this operation came through researcher discovery of files on an exposed server, not through the ministry's own detection. Thailand's cybersecurity authorities were notified after the fact. What would have caught this earlier was network monitoring that logs and alerts on unusual automated command execution, segmentation that restricts what compromised systems can access, and credential management that prevents default passwords from opening critical infrastructure to anyone who finds them.

summary:
# Summary

Thailand's Ministry of Finance was targeted by attackers using an AI agent called Hermes to conduct network reconnaissance and exploitation between June and July 2026. Researchers discovered three exposed directories on a Hong Kong server containing 585 files with exploit code, stolen credentials, and malware samples. The attackers deployed a custom Go implant named Hades across Windows and Linux systems and created custom tools to target the ministry's Hadoop data infrastructure, GlassFish application servers, and email systems using default credentials and known vulnerabilities.

The operation reveals a sophisticated Chinese-speaking threat actor with detailed knowledge of the ministry's internal network. The Hermes AI agent ran in unattended mode, automatically executing dangerous commands without human approval, while enumerating hosts and capturing privilege escalation data. Investigators identified four servers linked to the activity and recovered evidence showing the attackers accessed session cookies and internal administrative panels, though complete network compromise could not be confirmed. Thailand's national cybersecurity authorities were notified on July 15, 2026, and the findings were disclosed after a standard seven-day waiting period.
